Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Unmask persistence after AP-1 washout
ideas.description: Use an inducible AP-1 system (e.g., 4-OHT-activated FOS-ER or a dTAG-tagged JUN) to pulse AP-1 activity, then remove the inducer and track ATAC-seq, H3K27ac, and AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN) at target enhancers over days. If AP-1 is a memory mechanism, chromatin opening and reinduction capacity should persist after AP-1 protein returns to baseline. Analogy: like unmasking a latent signal once the noise has cleared, the stored state should be visible only after the active factor is gone.

ideas.title: Degron-timed erasure to separate maintenance from encoding
ideas.description: Apply acute AP-1 degradation (dTAG or auxin degron on JUN/FOS) at different times after priming: during induction, during a quiescent interval, and at late timepoints. If AP-1 is required only for encoding, degradation after the interval should not erase the memory, whereas continuous AP-1 requirement for maintenance would show loss of the primed response. Readout is the reinduction of target genes on re-stimulation. Analogy: like unrigging a mechanism at chosen moments to see which parts hold the stored state.

ideas.title: Savings assay with motif-mutant enhancers
ideas.description: Compare first- and second-exposure transcriptional kinetics (e.g., nascent RNA by TT-seq or smFISH) at endogenous loci, wild-type versus CRISPR-edited TGAGTCA (TRE) motifs in the enhancers. A memory role predicts faster or stronger second responses (savings) that disappear when the AP-1 site is mutated, while non-memory priming would not depend on the motif. Analogy: recoating a surface only works as a memory if the first coat left a lasting trace.

ideas.title: Lineage-tracked AP-1 reporter for heritable memory
ideas.description: Express a destabilized live reporter of AP-1 activity (e.g., FOS promoter-driven d2EGFP) in cells, then track single-cell lineages by time-lapse imaging across several divisions after a transient stimulus. Test whether prior AP-1 activity history predicts the magnitude of future responses in daughter cells, and whether that correlation decays with generation number. Analogy: the way a trait passes through successive generations, like a lineage of cells carrying a state forward.

ideas.title: Scrambled-motif and matched-control statistical design
ideas.description: Perform JUN/FOS ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN and H3K27ac profiling at matched timepoints after stimulus, comparing AP-1-bound sites to a control set of shuffled or scrambled TRE-like motifs and GC/accessibility-matched random genomic regions. A memory mechanism should show sustained, AP-1-motif-dependent signal at lasting sites that exceeds what generic priming produces at the controls. Analogy: a randomized word list as a null, so that any pattern found must be specific rather than an artifact of composition.
